title: Service Dependability Pilot Canvas and Weekly Journal
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures the lightweight pilot canvas and a weekly journal for the Service Dependability pilot (May–Jul 2026). Goal is to run a focused, cross-functional experiment that ties SLO definitions to explicit customer impact and operational runbooks we can use as a template for future launches. This is a working journal — expect shorthand, TODOs, and decisions logged as we go.

Scope:
- Target service: hosted-api-ingest (front-end request path for text generation).
- Pilot traffic: 5% canary of production traffic -> staged to 20% -> 50% -> fallback.
- Teams involved: SRE (lead), Serving Runtime, Platform, Product (Hosted API), Observability, Solutions Eng.
- Timebox: 12 weeks (experiment + analysis + roll-forward).

Customer-impact-driven SLOs (initial hypotheses):
1) Latency SLO — p95 end-to-end request latency < 250ms for short/text-generation-1 requests, 99.5% success over 30d window. Customer impact: interactive chat UX degradation if violated.
2) Availability SLO — request success rate (2xx/streaming OK) >= 99.9% over 30d. Customer impact: revenue and task completion for high-traffic customers.
3) Freshness SLO — model version switch latency (time to route to new pinned model) < 2m; target 99% of change events. Customer impact: predictable rollouts and minimal consistency windows.

Success metrics (what will convince us to adopt template):
- Clear mapping from SLO breach to customer-impact example (documented and tested with a sample customer scenario).
- Runbook actions reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for common failure modes by >= 30% vs baseline.
- Feature teams adopt the SLO template for 3 additional services within 90 days.

Pilot phases and key milestones:
- Phase 0 (Week -1 to 1): Scoping, signal readiness, baseline telemetry extraction, traffic mirroring.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 2–4): 5% canary + runbook dry runs, alert tuning, incident simulation tabletop.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–7): 20% canary, small customer beta, monitoring for false positives.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 8–10): 50% canary, split rollouts for model variants, runbook refinement.
- Phase 4 (Week 11–12): Final analysis, playbook handoff, and product decision (rollout / abort / rework).

Roles & RACI (high level):
- SRE (Aisha Patel) — overall pilot lead, runbook owner, incident coordinator (Accountable).
- Serving Runtime (Marcus Nguyen) — performance tuning, kernel/quantization experiment owner (Responsible).
- Observability (Claire Robertson) — metrics dashboards, SLO reporting, alert noise remediation (Responsible).
- Product Hosted API (Diego Morales) — stakeholder liaison, customer beta conduit (Consulted).
- Solutions Eng (Sana Iqbal) — drafts customer scenarios and acceptance tests (Consulted).
- Platform Eng — capacity provisioning and autoscaling policy adjustments (Informed/Responsible depending on change window).

Observability and instrumentation checklist (must be green before canary):
- Request-level tracing propagated (trace id across mesh).
- Per-customer tokenized error rates & latency histograms.
- Model-version routing events recorded with timestamps.
- Error budget dashboard with burn-rate window (1h/6h/30d).
- Alert definitions: p95-latency-warning (p95 > 200ms sustained 5m), p95-latency-critical (> 300ms 3m), request-success-rate-critical (< 99.8% 5m).

Runbook sketch (short):
Trigger: request-success-rate-critical fires.
1) Pager -> SRE oncall (primary).
2) Triage step (first 5m): check global traffic, model errors, downstream storage, recent rollouts.
3) Escalation (15m): engage Serving Runtime, Platform; consider emergency routing -> fallback model variant.
4) Mitigation action: automated rollback if new model variant deployed within last 10m OR add capacity via autoscale policy.
5) Postmortem owner assigned within 48h.

Canary traffic steering & automatic fallback policy (decision canvas):
- Default route weights: stable-model 95% / canary-model 5% at start.
- Fallback pause condition: error budget burn rate > 4x baseline over 30m AND p95 latency increase > 40%.
- Automatic rollback: if both conditions met for > 10m, shift 100% traffic to stable-model and open incident.

Weekly Journal (high-level entries):
- 2026-05-04 (kickoff): Aligned on scope; action: Observability to extract baseline metrics by 2026-05-10 (Claire). TODO: confirm list of customer scenarios (Sana).
- 2026-05-11: Baselines extracted; noticed p95 tails tied to queueing at frontend. Action: Serving Runtime to adjust worker batch-sizing; platform to reserve 2x extra burst nodes for canary.
- 2026-05-18 (dry run): Runbook tabletop conducted with Product + Solutions Eng. Findings: alert thresholds too tight -> increased false positives. Action: adjust p95-warning window to 5m sustained and add burn-rate filter.
- 2026-05-25 (5% canary launch): Initial canary saw small spike in model-variant errors (0.3% above baseline). Automated fallback triggered successfully. Decision: keep canary and file PR for logging fix. Owner: Marcus (PR #274).
- 2026-06-08 (20% canary): Observed burst periods where p95 moved to 320ms for specific shard sets. Mitigation: increase KV cache warmup and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. Action owner: Serving Runtime.
- 2026-06-22: Customer beta created for 2 pilot customers. Feedback: careful about rollouts during customer peak times; need quiet windows. Product to schedule rolling deploys.

Experiment variants we are testing:
- Quantization profile A vs B under identical requests (latency/cost tradeoff).
- Batching policy conservative vs aggressive (smaller latency variance vs throughput).
- Model routing: sticky vs stateless sticky (affects freshness SLO).

Open risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Observability gaps for per-tenant tails -> Mitigation: add per-tenant sampled tracing for top 20 customers before 20% canary. (Claire).
- Risk: Autoscaler lag during traffic spikes -> Mitigation: add pre-warm nodes and tune scale-out threshold (Platform).
- Risk: Too many alerts during early phases -> Mitigation: create temporary escalation channel (#dep-pilot-ops) and add human-in-loop for first 48 hours of each ramp.

Acceptance & rollout criteria checklist:
- SLO reporting displays baseline and current burn-rate (Observability green).
- Runbook validated in 2 tabletop sim scenarios without human error > 80% (dry run pass).
- Customer beta yields no high-severity incidents for 14 days at 20% traffic.
- Performance cost delta (cost per 1M tokens) acceptable to product (<= +15%).

Handoff artifacts to produce by end of pilot:
- Final SLO spec with customer-impact examples and measurement windows (doc).
- Complete runbook with decision tree and reroute automation steps (markdown + playbook).
- Postmortem template and sample postmortem from any incident in the pilot.
- Implementation guide: how to apply the template to another service (checklist).

Open questions (for leadership/product):
- What is an acceptable customer-facing degradation tolerance for experimental customers? (Product decision)
- Should runbooks be owned by SRE or split between SRE and feature teams for long-lived services?

Next actions (immediate):
- Claire to add per-tenant sampling dashboards by 2026-05-14 (DONE).
- Marcus to open PR for improved logging and error labeling (PR #274 — in flight).
- Platform to publish pre-warm node runbook and cost estimate by 2026-05-18.
- Aisha to schedule the next tabletop on 2026-05-20 and invite product beta customers.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the pilot narrow — better to have a complete, reproducible playbook for one service than a vague plan for many.
- Capture examples of customer-impact in plain language — product teams use these in sales / CS conversations.

References / Links:
- Confluence: DEP-PILOT Canvas (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira epic: JIRA-REL-4123 (pilot epic)
- GitHub: infra PR for logging and fallback: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/274
- Slack channel: #rel-dependability-pilot (create if not exists)

Appendix: short incident postmortem template (to copy into final deliverable):
- Incident title + timeline (UTC)
- Impacted customers and severity assessment
- Trigger / root cause hypothesis + data
- Immediate mitigations and timeline to resolution
- Corrective actions and owners (short + long term)
- Metrics to track post-fix (and who will follow up)

-- End of journal (working draft). Expect to refine after each phase; will convert to polished playbook once we reach Phase 4 and have one full mitigation cycle documented.
